text:
• Maharashtra – approved development of a ₹45 Cr Eco-Nature Park at Thane Creek Flamingo Sanctuary, Mumbai 
- It is India’s first AI-powered bird detection & monitoring centre, as part of Bhandup Bird Park project 
• District Planning Committee’s special fund – allocated ₹45 Cr for this sanctuary 
• Thane Creek Flamingo Sanctuary – declared a wildlife sanctuary in 2015, India’s 1st dedicated flamingo sanctuary 
- It is also designated a Ramsar site 
• Maharashtra: Capital – Mumbai  |  CM – Devendra Fadnavis  |  Governor – Jishnu Dev Varma

• Droupadi Murmu (India’s 15th President) – completed 4 years in office on Jul 25, 2026 
- She became India’s 1st tribal Head of State 
• She launched a series of citizen-centric, sustainability-focused & heritage initiatives at Rashtrapati Bhavan & President’s 
Estates 
• Key initiatives include: 
- Launch of an application-based e-Audio Guide for visitors to Rashtrapati Bhavan 
- Launch of 3rd edition of e-Upahaar, featuring 300 curated Presidential gifts for public auction 
• She also launched – ‘Bachpan Bal Parisar’, a new facility for children residing in President’s Estate 
- It comprises ‘Kilkari’, a dedicated play zone & ‘Samarth Anganwadi-cum-Palna’ 
• She also flagged off ‘RAAHI’, a fare -free, wheelchair-accessible, 27-seater electric bus service for staff & residents of 
President’s Estate 
- RAAHI – Rashtrapati Bhavan Access & Heritage Interconnector 
• C.P. Radhakrishnan (VP) – released 1st set of 5 commemorative books marking her 4 years in office

• As per MHA: 12,000+ e-Zero FIRs have been registered against cyber financial fraud cases over past year 
- Across 18 states & UTs that have implemented this system  |  Delhi – topped list 
• e-Zero FIR system – launched in May 2025 
- It allows victims of cyber financial fraud to report crimes directly online or through national helpline 
• Highest number of e-Zero FIRs – Delhi (6,115)  |  Followed by – Chandigarh (4,174), Uttarakhand (552) 
• ‘Police’ & ‘Public Order’ – State subjects under 7th Schedule of Constitution 
• Minister of Home Affairs: Amit Shah  |  Constituency – Gandhinagar, Gujarat 
MoS in Ministry of Home Affairs: Nityanand Rai & Bandi Sanjay Kumar

• Department of Expenditure enforced a ‘One Officer, One Official Car’ policy for bureaucracy 
- To curb misuse of govt vehicles, reduce public expenditure & ensure more efficient use of govt resources 
• An officer who has already been allotted an official vehicle will not be provided with a second government car 
• Under existing rules, entitled officers may use their official cars for limited personal travel of up to 500 km per month 
- By paying a fixed fee of ₹3,000 per month & forfeiting their standard monthly transport allowance

• Rajnath Singh – inaugurated Department of Military Medicine, at Command Hospital (Central Command), Lucknow, UP 
- Established under – Directorate General of Medical Services (Army) 
• It complements proposed Global Military Medicine Centre, envisioned under Raksha Strategy Vision 2026-30 
• Minister of Defence: Rajnath Singh  |  Constituency – Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh 
MoS in Ministry of Defence: Sanjay Seth

• MoPR – launched “DAANVEER” to strengthen digital infrastructure of Gram Panchayats across India 
• Launched by – Vivek Bharadwaj (Secretary, MoPR) 
• DAANVEER is developed in collaboration with – National Informatics Centre (NIC) & DigiHaat 
• Minister of Panchayati Raj: Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh)  |  Constituency – Munger, Bihar 
MoS in Ministry of Panchayati Raj: S. P. Singh Baghel

• I4C ordered GitHub to remove Bitchat, an open-source, Bluetooth-based, peer-to-peer messaging application 
- Citing – Section 79(3)(b) of Information Technology Act, 2000 & Rule 3(1)(d) of Information Technology Rules, 2021 
• It directed GitHub to disable access to 3 Bitchat repositories within 3 hours 
• Bitchat (created by Jack Dorsey ) – uses Bluetooth Low Energy mesh networks to enable encrypted communication 
between nearby devices 
• HQs of I4C – New Delhi  |  CEO – Rajesh Kumar

• GoI aims to develop a total of 44 airports, including 4 hub airports, to provide seamless international air connectivity 
• Presently, there is 1 hub airport (Delhi) & 2 spoke airports (Varanasi & Amritsar) 
• This model is designed to enable seamless connectivity between Tier-II & Tier-III airports & international destinations 
• Under this model, Air India introduced ‘Easy Connect’ flights 
- It enables travellers from cities beyond major hubs to check in, drop baggage & complete immigration formalities 
at their origin airport

• MoHUA approved projects for 6 urban development initiatives in Ahmedabad  |  Worth – ₹2,719.80 Cr 
- Under Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), a flagship scheme initiated by PM Modi 
• Approved projects include: ₹852.93 Cr – for rehabilitation of main sewerage network in West Ahmedabad 
- ₹551.35 Cr – for rehabilitation of main sewerage network in East Ahmedabad 
- ₹290.24 Cr – for rehabilitation of old sewerage networks in various parts of city 
- ₹215 Cr – for an Intelligent Water Management System 
- ₹479.25 Cr – for a 125 TPD (tonnes per day) Integrated Sludge Management Facility 
- ₹331.03 Cr – for an Integrated Transit Management System (ITMS) & Automated Fare Collection System (AFCS) 
• Urban Challenge Fund – approved by Cabinet in Feb 2026 
- It is designed to facilitate a total investment of ₹4 lakh Cr in India’s urban sector over next 5 years (FY26 to FY31) 
- UCF – a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with a total Central Assistance of ₹1 lakh Cr 
• It includes a Credit Repayment Guarantee Sub -Scheme, providing a central guarantee of up to ₹7 Cr or 70% of loan 
amount 
• Minister of Housing & Urban Affairs: Manohar Lal Khattar  |  Constituency – Karnal, Haryana 
MoS in Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs: Tokhan Sahu

• SC – issued interim order barring posting, reposting, uploading, extraction, modification, dissemination or monetisation 
of audio-video recordings of court proceedings on social media & other digital platforms 
- Without prior permission of SG of Supreme Court or Registrar Generals of concerned High Courts 
• It was issued by a 3-judge bench comprising CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi & Justice V. Mohana 
• Present CJI of Supreme Court – Justice Surya Kant (53rd)  |  Established on – Jan 26, 1950 
Retirement age: Chief Justices & Judges of HC – 62 years  |  CJI & judges of the SC – 65 years 
Sanctioned strength of judges in the SC – 38 (including CJI)

• Kerala began integrating ANNAM.AI smart weather stations under its 100-day action plan for climate-smart agriculture 
- It marks state’s rollout of a Centre of Excellence for AI in Agriculture initiative developed at IIT Ropar 
• Punjab – 1st implementation location, where 100 AI-powered weather stations were deployed by Mar 30, 2026 
• ANNAM.AI plans to train 10,000 students, rural youth & agriculture professionals in use of AI applications in agriculture 
• ANNAM.AI + Syngenta = to focus on crop health monitoring, pest outbreak tracking & heat-stress management 
- During Bharat Innovates 2026 – held in France  (in Jun 2026) 
• Kerala: Capital – Thiruvananthapuram  |  CM – V D Satheesan  |  Governor – Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar

• Ladakh – declared 23 heritage sites as “Protected Monuments” under J&K Ancient Monuments Preservation Act 
• Prominent monuments notified include: Petroglyph Site at Sharnos  |  Tingmosgang Fort  |  Ancient Caves at Saspol 
- Maitreya Buddha Rock Carving at Shey near Sindhu Ghat  |  Petroglyph sites at Domkhar, Lehdo, Alchi & Murgi 
- Stongday Gonpa  |  Meditation Cave of Onpo at Hunder  |  Hunder Cave  |  Dechen Tsomo Khar (Fort) 
- Stampuk Cave  |  Rock-Carved Buddha Statue at Hunder  |  Rigsum Gonbo Rock Carvings at Diggar  |  Sumoor Fort 
- Chamba Karpo (White Maitreya Buddha) at Diggar  |  Rock Inscriptions at Yourbaltak in Kargil 
- Petroglyph Site at Mangmore in Kargil 
• Ladakh: Capital – Leh  |  Lieutenant Governor – Vinai Kumar Saxena

• Rajasthan – became India’s 1st state to execute Exploration Licence for Rare Earth Elements (REEs) & associated minerals, 
strengthening access to critical mineral resources 
• Exploration Licence – covers 207.63 sq. km. Navatala -Devigarh region across Pachpadra tehsil (Balotra district) & 
Shergarh tehsil (Jodhpur district), western Rajasthan 
• The licence has been granted to – M/s Central Mine Planning and Design Institute Limited (CMPDI) 
• REEs identified – Lanthanum, Cerium, Praseodymium & Neodymium 
• Rajasthan – became 1st state to operationalise an auctioned exploration licence block in India  
- also ranks 1st in auction of major mineral blocks 
• Rajasthan: Capital – Jaipur  |  CM – Bhajan Lal Sharma  |  Governor – Haribhau Kisanrao Bagde

• Brookfield – launched “Lumara”, a dedicated renewable energy platform in India 
- with planned investment of ~$600 million for solar, wind & Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects 
• Funding – backed by Brookfield’s Catalytic Transition Fund (CTF)  
- launched with anchor commitment from UAE-backed climate investment vehicle “ALTÉRRA”  (corpus – up to $5 bn) 
• Platform objective – address renewable energy deployment challenges including PPA negotiation delays, grid 
connection queues & land acquisition timelines 
• Brookfield India portfolio – ~45 GW combined wind & solar capacity across operational & under-development projects  
• India renewable energy target – 500 GW installed renewable energy capacity by 2030 
• Nawal Saini – Managing Partner & Head of Energy for South Asia and the Middle East at Brookfield 
• HQs of Brookfield – New York, USA (also headquartered in Toronto, Canada)  |  CEO – Bruce Flatt

• India observed 16ᵗʰ Indian Organ Donation Day event in New Delhi  (The day is observed on August 3) 
- Organised by – National Organ & Tissue Transplant Organisation (NOTTO)  
• Govt launched ‘Jug Jug Jiyo Abhiyaan’ alongside ‘e-Pratyaropan’ (e-प्रत्यारोपण) portal & ‘NOTTO’ mobile application 
• Govt also released ‘National Brain Stem Death Certification Guidelines’ & ‘National Guidelines on Swap Transplantation’ 
- To standardise procedures across States & UTs 
• As per NOTTO Annual Report 2025-26, India performed 20,138 organ transplants in 2025  (highest in a single year) 
• India now ranks 3ʳᵈ globally in total organ transplants  |  Top – United States & China 
• India crossed 5 lakh Aadhaar-verified organ donation pledges since launch of national digital pledge portal in 2023 
• Best State for recording highest number of deceased organ donors – Tamil Nadu (266) 
- Followed by – Maharashtra (205), Telangana (198), Karnataka (154) & Kerala (152) 
• Best State award for North Eastern Region – Assam  |  Best Union Territory – Delhi 
• Best Regional Organ & Tissue Transplant Organisation (Northern Region) – PGIMER Chandigarh

• Indian Railways – transported a live donor heart by train for 1ˢᵗ time in India’s history 
- Aboard “Vande Bharat Express” (Train No. 20901 - Mumbai Central-Gandhinagar Capital) 
- Ensuring timely arrival for transplantation at U.N. Mehta Institute of Cardiology & Research Centre, Ahmedabad 
• A dedicated ‘Green Corridor’ was created from Platform No. 1 of Ahmedabad Railway Station to U.N. Mehta Institute of 
Cardiology & Research Centre 
- Jointly managed by – RPF & Gujarat Police 
• HQs of Indian Railways – New Delhi  |  Chairman & CEO – Satish Kumar

• PM Modi inaugurated & laid foundation stone of multiple development, technology & cultural infrastructure projects 
• In Andhra Pradesh: 
- He dedicated multiple development projects worth over ₹17,900 Cr in Bhogapuram 
- He inaugurated Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district 
o It is developed under Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode at a cost of over ₹5,640 Cr 
- He also laid foundation stone of Andhra Semiconductor & Innovation Park Semiconductor Project at Visakhapatnam 
o Investment – ₹460 Cr  (Andhra Pradesh’s 1ˢᵗ semiconductor manufacturing facility) 
• In Karnataka: 
- He inaugurated ‘Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre - Viveka Smaraka’ at Sri Ramakrishna Ashrama 
• Andhra Pradesh: Capital – Amaravati  |  CM – N Chandra Babu Naidu  |  Governor – Syed Abdul Nazeer 
• Karnataka: Capital – Bangalore  |  CM – D. K. Shivakumar  |  Governor – Thaawarchand Gehlot

• PM Modi launched “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan” in Aug 2026 
• It connected over 1 Cr young citizens from more than 28,000 locations across the country

• 4ᵗʰ edition of ‘Tri-Services Future Warfare Course’ – commenced at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi 
• It is being conducted under aegis of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) 
- Coordinated by – Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS) 
• 1st edition – held in Sep 2024

• Glaw Lake (Arunachal Pradesh’s 1st Ramsar Site) – designated India’s 101st Ramsar Site 
• It is nestled within Kamlang Tiger Reserve & WS at an elevation of 1,168 metres in densely forested Eastern Himalayas 
• Glaw Lake is a pristine freshwater lake & recognised biodiversity hotspot 
• Ramsar Convention – signed in Ramsar, Iran, in 1971 
• India’s Ramsar network – rose to 101 Ramsar Sites in 2026  (from 26 Ramsar Sites in 2014) 
• Arunachal Pradesh: Capital – Itanagar  |  CM – Pema Khandu  |  Governor – Lt. Gen. Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik

• IIT Hyderabad + CEEPL = launched “ANUGYAN”, a Nuclear Technology Orientation Programme (NTOP) 
- Formally launched during a ceremony held at IIT Hyderabad campus at Kandi in Sangareddy, Telangana 
• It is open to engineering graduates, working professionals, PSU executives, EPC  contractors & industrial equipment 
manufacturers 
• Director of IIT Hyderabad – Prof. Budaraju Srinivasa Murty 
• HQs of CEEPL – New Delhi  |  CMD – Cdr. Binu Tom Jacob

• Supreme Court of India – directed that mandatory 3rd-party insurance period for new vehicles be extended by 1 year 
- New cars must be covered for 4 years & new 2-wheelers for 6 years at time of purchase 
• Present CJI of Supreme Court – Justice Surya Kant (53rd)  |  Established on – Jan 26, 1950 
- Retirement age: Chief Justices & Judges of HC – 62 years  |  CJI & judges of the SC – 65 years 
- Sanctioned strength of judges in the SC – 38 (including CJI)

• Telangana Police launched Next-Generation Telangana Emergency Response Support System (TG-ERSS) - Dial 112 
- It is an AI-powered integrated emergency response platform 
- Inaugurated by – DGP C.V. Anand, at Telangana Integrated Command & Control Centre (TGiCCC) in Hyderabad 
• It integrates Police, Fire Services, Ambulance Services, Women Safety, Child Protection, Disaster Response & other 
emergency services under single national emergency number 112 
• Its centre operates on a 24×7 basis with 164 trained personnel & 900 SIP-based communication channels 
• Telangana’s average emergency response time – 10 minutes & 30 seconds statewide 
- National average – 18 minutes 
• Telangana Police plans to introduce AI -enabled drones on a pilot basis in Hyderabad, Cyberabad, Malkajgiri & Future 
City Commissionerates 
• Telangana: Capital – Hyderabad  |  CM – A. Revanth Reddy  |  Governor – Shiv Pratap Shukla

• MHA formally included heatwaves & lightning in list of notified natural calamities for award period 2026-31 
- Under ‘Operational Guidelines for Administration of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)’ & ‘National Disaster 
Response Fund (NDRF)’ 
• It makes states eligible for financial assistance under Disaster Management Act, 2005 
• Now, list of notified natural calamities has expanded to 14 categories  (from 12) 
- Cyclone, drought, earthquake, flood, tsunami, avalanche, cloudburst, landslide, hailstorm, fire, frost/cold wave, pest 
attack, heatwave & lightning 
• Lightning is responsible for largest number of deaths due to any single disaster reported in India 
• Highest number of cases recorded (heatwaves) – Telangana (915) 
- Followed by – West Bengal (733), Chhattisgarh (660) & Andhra Pradesh (540) 
• Highest number of confirmed heatstroke deaths – Maharashtra 
• Minister of Home Affairs: Amit Shah  |  Constituency – Gandhinagar, Gujarat 
MoS in Ministry of Home Affairs: Nityanand Rai & Bandi Sanjay Kumar

• India – developed an integrated, intelligence-led & technology-driven model to combat fugitive criminals 
- Under which India has brought back 274 fugitive criminals from 36 countries between 2019 & 2026 
• Govt enacted ‘Fugitive Economic Offenders Act in 2018’ to strengthen action against fugitives 
- Under which assets of ₹17,874 Cr belonging to fugitive criminals have been attached through enforcement of PMLA 
- Assets of ₹18,762 Cr has been returned in cases involving Fugitive Economic Offenders 
• Govt also enacted NIA (Amendment) Act & UAPA (Amendment) Act in 2019 & introduced 3 new criminal laws in 2024

• MoH&FW deployed a ‘National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT)’ to Gujarat & Rajasthan 
- To strengthen response to ongoing Chandipura Virus Disease (CHPV) outbreak 
• NJORT comprises experts from NCDC, ICMR & DAHD 
• NCDC’s Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) – also activated to support NJORT 
• Chandipura virus – first identified in 1965 after being isolated from febrile patients in Chandipur village, Maharashtra 
• Gujarat: Capital – Gandhinagar  |  CM – Bhupendra Patel  |  Governor – Acharya Dev Vrat 
• Rajasthan: Capital – Jaipur  |  CM – Bhajan Lal Sharma  |  Governor – Haribhau Kisanrao Bagde 
• Minister of Health & Family Welfare: Jagat Prakash Nadda  |  Constituency – Gujarat 
MoS in Ministry of Health & Family Welfare: Jadhav Prataprao Ganpatrao & Anupriya Singh Patel

• C.P. Radhakrishnan launched ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan’ in Andaman & Nicobar Islands 
- By hoisting National Flag at Flag Point, Sri Vijaya Puram 
• Andaman & Nicobar Islands: Capital – Sri Vijaya Puram  |  Lieutenant Governor – Adm D K Joshi

• India crossed a landmark 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel-based electricity generation capacity 
- Total non-fossil fuel capacity – 300.50 GW  (as on Jul 31, 2026) 
• Share of non-fossil fuel electricity capacity in India’s total installed electricity generation capacity – 552 GW  (over 54%) 
• Total non-fossil fuel capacity (300.50 GW) comprises: Solar power – 164.59 GW  |  Wind power – 58.14 GW 
- Hydro power – 57.24 GW  |  Bio-power – 11.75 GW  |  Nuclear power – 8.78 GW 
• During 2025-26, India added 55.29 GW of non-fossil fuel-based electricity generation capacity 
- Contribution: Solar – 44.6 GW  |  Wind – 6 GW 
• Renewable electricity generation – rose to 477.79 BU in 2025-26  (from 190.96 billion units (BU) in 2014-15)

• NeGD (MeitY) + AAERI = partnered to launch ‘AAERI Verify’, a digital platform integrated directly with DigiLocker 
- To enable secure, paperless & consent-based verification of academic, identity & financial documents for Indian 
students applying to Australian universities 
• It was officially unveiled during AAERI Annual Convention in New Delhi on Aug 7, 2026 
• It replaces slow, manual document verification with a secure 2-stage strategic framework:

• “E-Samudra” – launched in India to strengthen seafarer welfare, security & service delivery 
- It is a digital platform integrating services for seafarers, shipping companies, ports & other maritime stakeholders 
into a single digital window 
• Inaugurated by – Sarbananda Sonowal (MoPSW) 
- During “Seafarer Security, Safety and Welfare and Inauguration of E-Samudra” held in Mumbai on Aug 8, 2026 
- Organised by – Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) 
• India’s active seafarer workforce – grown to more than 3.23 lakh in 2025  (from about 1.03 lakh in 2013) 
• DGMA showcased a series of initiatives to modernise maritime administration, including: 
- e-NAVIK 24x7 grievance redressal system  |  Seafarer Tracking Dashboard 
- Digital Seafarers Employment Agreement  |  Enhanced welfare measures under Seafarers Welfare Fund Society

• Oilseed production in India – rose to 43.06 million tonnes in 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimate)  (from 39 MTs in 2022-23) 
• Domestic availability of edible oils – increased to 126.30 lakh tonnes in 2024-25  (from 124.23 lakh tonnes in 2022-23) 
- Edible oil imports (over same period) – declined to 160.72 lakh tonnes  (from 165.00 lakh tonnes) 
• During 2025-26, GoI distributed free quality seeds covering 13.52 lakh hectares under Value Chain Clusters 
• India’s cumulative oil palm area – 6.40 lakh hectares  (as of Mar 31, 2026) 
• National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) – approved on Oct 3, 2024 
- Aim: To increase India’s primary oilseed production from 39 MTs (2022-23) to 69.7 MTs by 2030-31 
• National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) – launched in Aug 2021  |  Total outlay – ₹11,040 Cr 
- Aim: To reduce India’s heavy dependence on imported edible oils

• MHA issued new national security guidelines banning solar, wind & hybrid renewable energy projects within 1 km of 
LoC, LAC & International Border (IB) 
• A wider band extending up to 50 km from LoC, LAC International Border has been classified as a “sensitive area” 
• Projects between 1 km & 20 km of International Border will additionally require an NOC from MoD 
• MHA also imposed height restrictions on project-related civil infrastructure in these sensitive zones: 
- Up to 3 metres – within 1-8 km band  |  Up to 5 metres – between 8-20 km  |  Up to 15 metres – between 20-50 km 
• Minister of Home Affairs: Amit Shah  |  Constituency – Gandhinagar, Gujarat 
MoS in Ministry of Home Affairs: Nityanand Rai & Bandi Sanjay Kumar

• HAL Airport (Bengaluru) – became 1st airport in India to operationalise Required Navigation Performance -Category H 
(RNP CAT H) helicopter approach 
- Developed by – AAI  |  Approved by – DGCA 
- Validated through flight trials conducted by – HAL test pilots 
• HQs of AAI – New Delhi  |  Chairman – Vipin Kumar 
• HQs of HAL – Bengaluru, Karnataka  |  CMD – Ravi Kota

• India’s honey production – increased to 1,51,690 metric tonnes (MT) in 2025-26  (from 80,530 MT in 2014-15) 
• India exported around 1.07 lakh MT of natural honey worth $177.55 million in FY24 
- It makes India 2nd-largest exporter of honey globally  (from 9th rank in 2020) 
• Since 2021-22, Centre supported 21 beekeeping projects in West Bengal alone under NBHM  |  Outlay – ₹16.13 Cr 
• WB – produced 24.05 thousand MT of honey in FY26 as per 2nd Advance Estimates of Horticulture Crops Statistics 
• National Beekeeping & Honey Mission (NBHM) – a Central Sector Scheme approved by GoI 
- Total budget outlay – ₹500 Cr for period FY21 to FY26  |  NBHM operates through 3 Mini Missions 
- It is being implemented by – Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare through National Bee Board (NBB)

• Gujarat approved establishment of 4 Centres of Excellence (CoEs) for natural farming in Navsari, Morbi, Bhavnagar & 
Chhota Udepur districts 
- It allocates ₹20 Cr for initiative in 2026-27 
• In 1st phase, the Centres will be established at: Nani Bhamti village in Vansda taluka of Navsari, Halvad in Morbi district 
- Valavad village in Sihor taluka of Bhavnagar  |  Chudel village in Jetpur Pavi taluka of Chhota Udepur 
• Implementing agency for this scheme – Gujarat Prakrutik Krishi Vikas Board 
• Gujarat: Capital – Gandhinagar  |  CM – Bhupendra Patel  |  Governor – Acharya Dev Vrat

• Assam – recorded world’s 1st-ever release of captive -bred Slender-billed Vultures (Gyps tenuirostris) fitted with GSM -
GPS satellite transmitters 
- 10 captive-bred vultures (5 Slender-billed Vultures & 5 White-rumped Vultures) were soft-released 
- From Jatayu Aviary at Tewaripal in Biswanath Wildlife Division of Kaziranga National Park & Tiger Reserve 
• This initiative is a joint programme of = Assam Forest Department + Kaziranga NP & TR + Bombay Natural History Society 
• Slender-billed Vulture & White-rumped Vulture – both are classified as ‘Critically Endangered’ 
• India recorded 9 species of vultures 
• Assam: Capital – Dispur  |  CM – Himanta Biswa Sarma  |  Governor – Lakshman Prasad Acharya

• MHA notified 11 more international ports enabling entry of e-visa-holder foreigners into India 
- Now, total number of international ports authorised for e-visa entry – 88 (37 airports, 38 seaports & 13 land ports) 
• Newly added 11 international ports include 9 land ports & 2 airports (Bhopal & Tirupati) 
- 9 land ports – Agartala, Darranga, Gede, Ghojadanga, Haridaspur, Jaigaon, Dawki, Moreh & Attari (Road) 
• India process approximately 95% of e-visa applications within 72 hours 
• India introduced e-Visa facility with an Electronic Travel Authorisation in 2014, initially covering nationals of 43 countries 
- It is currently available to citizens of 172 countries 
• Minister of Home Affairs: Amit Shah  |  Constituency – Gandhinagar, Gujarat 
MoS in Ministry of Home Affairs: Nityanand Rai & Bandi Sanjay Kumar

• TRAI expanded 1600-number series beyond BFSI sector to utilities, courier & logistics service providers 
- They will use a new ‘1601’ series to prevent fraud & impersonation & help consumers identify legitimate calls 
• Under Phase -I, 1601 series will be issued to electricity distribution companies, water utilities, city gas distribution 
companies, LPG distribution entities & other utility service providers, as well as courier companies 
• TSPs have been directed to complete migration & onboarding of eligible entities within 90 days from date of order 
• HQs of TRAI – New Delhi  |  Chairman – Anil Kumar Lahoti  |  Established in – 1997

• Flipkart Minutes – entered gourmet grocery segment with a range of premium & speciality food products 
- It launched its own private label brand, “Pykd”, to strengthen its position  |  It is being piloted first in Bengaluru 
• FirstClub (Bengaluru) – raised $55 million in its Series B funding round in Jun 2026 
• HQs of Flipkart – Bangalore, Karnataka  |  Chairperson & CEO – Kalyan Krishnamurthy

• VOC Port Authority (VOCPA) – became 1st port in India to be accredited with ISO 50001:2018 Certification 
- For its Energy Management System  |  Awarded by – Indian Register Quality Systems (IRQS) 
• This certification is guided by – ‘Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines’ of Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways 
• VOCPA had earlier become India’s 1st Major Port to secure both Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) Platinum Rating & 
Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) Shunya certification 
- It has separately been recognised as India’s 1st major port to achieve Scope-2 emission-free status

• MoPSW approved a ₹334.89 Cr internal flyover at Visakhapatnam Port Authority to improve cargo evacuation 
- Project was appraised by – Delegated Investment Board  (chaired by Secretary, MoPSW)  |  Length – 3.584-km 
- It will connect Convent Junction with Dock Area 
• Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways: Sarbananda Sonowal  |  Constituency – Dibrugarh, Assam 
MoS in Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways: Shantanu Thakur

• “Poshan Tracker” digital application – rolled out by MoWCD as an ICT-based governance tool 
- For continuous monitoring & tracking of all services provided to beneficiaries registered at Anganwadi Centres 
- Under ‘Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0)’ 
• Poshan Tracker – originally launched on Mar 1, 2021, through National e-Governance Division (NeGD) 
- It is available in 24 languages, including Hindi & English 
• A Facial Recognition System (FRS) – also integrated into Poshan Tracker for distribution of Take-Home Rations 
• MoWCD + MoHFW = jointly released a Protocol for Management of Malnutrition in Children 
- To prevent & treat severe acute malnutrition & reduce associated morbidity & mortality 
• Poshan Tracker initiative – received National Award for e-Governance 2024 (Gold) 
- For Government Process Re-engineering & Digital Transformation 
• Minister of Women & Child Development: Annpurna Devi  |  Constituency – Kodarma, Jharkhand 
MoS in Ministry of Women and Child Development: Savitri Thakur

• India’s exports from Special Economic Zones (SEZs) – rose 11.8% y-o-y to ₹16,36,192 Cr in 2025-26 
- Exports from these zones – ₹14,63,669 Cr in 2024-25 
• Outbound shipments from SEZs – ₹13.55 lakh Cr in 2023-24, ₹12.63 lakh Cr in 2022-23 & ₹9,90,747 Cr in 2021-22 
• Highest exports were recorded by – Gujarat (₹4,05,595 Cr) 
- Followed by – Karnataka (₹2,69,004 Cr), Maharashtra (₹2,43,422.50 Cr) & Tamil Nadu (₹2,12,288 Cr)

• Supreme Court clarified that its original interim order of Feb 14, 2024, will apply for sake of parity to notified wetland & 
community conservation reserves across India, not just to Asan reserve 
- It restricted mining activities within a 10-km radius of Asan Wetland Conservation Reserve in Uttarakhand 
• Mining activities within a 10-km radius of any such notified reserve must obtain prior approval from Standing Committee 
of National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) and/or MoEFCC before proceeding

• This amendment introduces four key changes to ‘Immigration and Foreigners Rules, 2025’ 
- Foreigners on visas valid for 180 days or less who wish to extend their stay must now complete registration at any

Immigration within 30 days of receiving order 
- Requirement to inform registration officer within 30 days of a child’s birth in India has been removed in cases where 
at least one parent is an Indian citizen & family wishes to retain child’s Indian citizenship 
o However, if child subsequently acquires foreign citizenship while residing in India, either parent must notify
